description: A localized skin infection caused by Bacillus anthracis, usually acquired through contact with infected animals or animal products.
symptoms: Painless ulcer with black eschar may develop
risk_factors: Occupational or environmental exposure to infected animals or contaminated animal products

appearance.general: A papule progresses to a vesicle or ulcer with a characteristic black eschar and surrounding oedema.

warning_signs: Rapidly increasing swelling, systemic illness, fever, or suspected occupational exposure requires urgent medical assessment.
doctor_discussion_points: Discuss animal exposure, occupational history, and timing of lesion development.
